title: Painting People in Rural France
content: Ohio-born artist Elizabeth Nourse painted directly from models in rural France. She was often "in villages with no inns or accommodations and lived either with members of a religious community or with the peasants, to an innate sympathy with women and children of the peasantry and enabled her to gain their confidence and observe them closely while living among them.""Cecilia Beaux(1855-1942) had quite a different experience in Brittany. Writing about her unsuccessful efforts to get a Breton woman to pose for her, she observed, 'We found that the people, especially the country folk, did not really likeles artistes.'"Quotes fromElisabeth Nourse, 1859-1938, A Salon CareerSource: Wikipedia onElizabeth NourseandCecilia Beaux
